reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Tally table of Favorite Ice Cream]

A teacher asked 30 students in her class the flavor of their favorite ice cream. The table above shows how the teacher recorded the students' responses.

In the bar graph below, which ice cream flavor corresponds to the bar that is labeled X?

[Image: Bar graph of Favorite Ice Cream]
reference_items.figure_description:
The item contains two visual elements:
1. A two-column table titled "Favorite Ice Cream" and "Number of Students":
   - Butterscotch: 4 single vertical tally marks (4)
   - Chocolate: 2 groups of 5 tally marks (10)
   - Strawberry: 1 group of 5 tally marks and 4 single vertical tally marks (9)
   - Vanilla: 1 group of 5 tally marks and 2 single vertical tally marks (7)
2. A vertical bar graph titled "Favorite Ice Cream":
   - The vertical axis is labeled "Number of Students" with grid lines at 2, 4, 6, 8, and 10.
   - The horizontal axis is labeled "Ice Cream Flavor".
   - There are 4 shaded vertical bars from left to right:
     - First bar has height 10.
     - Second bar is labeled "X" below the horizontal axis and has height 9.
     - Third bar has height 7.
     - Fourth bar has height 4.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration.
